hypotheses.title: Sales growth and earnings yield add to surprise persistence when forecasting the next earnings innovation
hypotheses.question: Before the next report, does a bounded rank model of niq_su, sale_gr1 and ni_me forecast the panel's next standardized earnings surprise better than current-surprise persistence, and does that belief translate into next-month excess return?
hypotheses.mechanism: Investors underanticipate persistence in operating changes: sales growth and profitability carry information about the next innovation that the current surprise alone does not, and prices may adjust slowly to the resulting earnings news.
falsification: Candidate rank IC against the target is not above the persistence baseline on the design partition.
The improvement appears in only one half of the evaluated months or in a single calendar year.
The belief improves but next-month return IC or the net tail spread after the flat cost is not positive.
The improvement disappears after within-sector neutralization.

hypotheses.title: Net equity issuance intensity is forecastable and its direction is underpriced
hypotheses.question: Does a bounded rank model of eqnetis_at, be_me and ret_12_1 forecast issuance intensity six months ahead better than current intensity alone, and does predicted heavy issuance precede lower next-month excess return?
hypotheses.mechanism: Issuance is an observable, dated capital-allocation decision; heavy issuers tend to keep financing and dilute value, and investors underweight the consequences of persistent dilution.
falsification: Candidate rank IC against future issuance intensity is not above the current-intensity baseline.
The predicted-issuance ranking does not carry a negative next-month return relation (bridge sign -1) after the flat cost.
The effect is explained by size, book-to-market or momentum exposure rather than issuance.
The improvement is concentrated in one year or one sector.

hypotheses.title: Valuation and earnings yield forecast sector-residual three-month returns beyond sector-relative value
hypotheses.question: Does a bounded rank model of be_me and ni_me forecast three-month sector-residual excess return better than sector-relative book-to-market alone, and is the translation positive after costs?
hypotheses.mechanism: Prices can misrepresent the durability of business economics; cheap valuation combined with earnings yield may identify firms priced for a worse outcome than observable evidence supports, beyond the generic value style.
falsification: Candidate rank IC is not above sector-relative book-to-market on the design partition.
The result is explained by generic value, size or momentum exposure.
The net tail spread after the flat cost is not positive or is below the baseline tail spread.
The improvement exists in only one half of the evaluated months.

hypotheses.title: Reversal, momentum and dollar volume forecast next-month sector-residual returns beyond simple reversal
hypotheses.question: Does a bounded rank model of ret_1_0, ret_12_1 and dolvol_126d forecast next-month sector-residual excess return better than short-term reversal alone, and does it survive the flat cost with realistic turnover?
hypotheses.mechanism: Temporary price pressure reverses and information diffuses slowly; liquidity conditions modulate both effects, so combining reversal, momentum and trading volume may identify temporary dislocations.
falsification: Candidate rank IC is not above the simple reversal baseline.
The net tail spread after the flat cost is not positive because turnover absorbs the gross spread.
The score is mostly a size or liquidity exposure.
The improvement is concentrated in one year or a few sectors.
